science.qualification: Photosphere color from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum, dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 3,540 K and log g 4.37 (u1 0.476, u2 0.311): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. The disc is unresolved: no map or absolute brightness is implied. Self-luminous, so no lighting.

science.label: Sector 95
science.description: Brightness of the star's surface that reproduces its light as it turns once in 4.85 days, fitted with starry to the light curve this project measured from the TESS full-frame images of sector 95 (the light swings by 8.5%; the map's curve leaves a scatter of 0.53%, the light's own noise being 0.17%). A light curve fixes how bright each longitude is, not the latitude of what darkens it. The map is made at a tilt of 71°, worked out from the star's rotation speed, period and radius. Gaia DR3 lists 16 other stars within 63 arcseconds, giving 0.29% of the light in the star's pixels. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · brightness map made here · Sector 95

science.label: Color + brightness
science.description: The star's color (#ffc08b, its Color dataset) over the brightness map this project made from the star's light in TESS sector 95 (July and August 2025): the map's scale, 85% to 115% of the mean surface, runs from a darker, richer tone of the same hue to the color itself. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the parts can be told apart: the darkest part gives 20.9% less light than the brightest. Longitudes are fixed by the light curve; latitudes and shapes are not. No color change of the spots is drawn: none is measured. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · the star in its color over its brightness map · July and August 2025
